In this section of the appendix, we extend the NFFRCISTG model described in @sec-network-causal-inference by allowing for the inclusion of two classes of observational unit — people and places — and by allowing the relationships between people and places to be randomly generated by the causal model.  
We name this the **Bipartite Random Network FFRCISTG model (BRNFFRCISTG)**.  It is a causal model that includes one or more *network generators* — structural equations that model the network edges as random variables.  

Before outlining the BRNFFRCISTG, we introduce new tools to mirror the shift we advocate from conceiving of statistical inference as the task of inferring something about a probability distribution using a growing number of realizations, to thinking about it as the task of inferring something about the distribution using one growing realization of the model.  We introduce the **causal Directed Acyclic Network Graph (DANG)** and the **Single World Intervention Network Graph (SWING)**.
